page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.large is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the proprietary ARM64-based Alibaba YiTian710 processor. The virtual machine provisioned on a KVM hypervisor features two dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.75 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory allocation includes 8.0 GB of RAM, preserving a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware cryptographic acceleration via ARM AES instructions. The configuration does not include local storage or discrete graphics processing units, relying entirely on remote block storage, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects performance characteristics typical of low-core count ARM servers. Single-core throughput shows competitive baseline efficiency, recording a stress-ng score of 1818.78 and compression throughput of 28.38 GB/sec in gzip, both rating within the median industry range. In contrast, overall multi-core compute capability is constrained by the two-core ceiling, yielding a multi-core stress-ng result of 3601.68 and a total PassMark CPU rating of 1734.7. Memory testing demonstrates uncached sequential read and write speeds of 38.93 GB/sec and 15.18 GB/sec respectively, alongside a Redis SET throughput of 3.45 million operations per second and static web transfer rates of 3.62 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, ecs.g8y.large serves as an entry-tier ARM deployment optimized for consistent dedicated CPU execution rather than burstable or heavy parallel processing. Its balanced memory footprint supports entry-level enterprise utility. The server is suited for lightweight microservices, small web servers, staging environments, basic Redis caching, and foundational development stacks that do not require intense mathematical vector computing or local NVMe storage arrays.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.large is a general-purpose ARM64 virtual server powered by Alibaba's custom YiTian710 processor. Configured on a KVM hypervisor, it provides two dedicated physical cores operating at 2.75 GHz alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. The architecture provides 64 MB of L3 cache and hardware AES encryption support. The instance includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached volumes and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average single-thread compute and compression rates, but aggregate multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth are limited by the two-core capacity. With predictable dedicated execution and balanced resource allocation, the server is suited for lightweight application hosting, containerized microservices, small Redis cache instances, and continuous integration agents.
